newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bond yields stick to lows,eager for CPI.
newsitem.headline: Australian bond yields stick to lows,eager for CPI.

text.p: *Australian bond yields stuck to their initial lows in the aftermath of Wednesday's strong rally in U.S. Treasuries.
*Market seen well-supported ahead of next week's key inflation data after its recent local currency-led shake-out.
Australian bond yields stuck to their initial lows in the aftermath of Wednesday's strong rally in U.S. Treasuries and as the Australian dollar put in a tentative rally.

The 10-year bond futures contract edged to a fresh 3-1/2 year high of 93.445 going into the lunchtime recess as it built on the rally seen in after hours trading and extended the rebound from Wednesday's low to some 20 basis points.
Traders the market was seen in better shape after its recent shake-out and futures were expected to move higher going into next week's second quarter inflation report.
U.S. yields remained around Wednesday's lower New York levels in early Tokyo trade following the modest 0.1 percent rise in the June CPI to an annual rate of 2.3 percent.

The data was seen lessening the chances of the Federal Reserve tightening in August, although the markets will get an update on the Fed's current policy thinking when chairman Alan Greenspan delivers his Humphrey-Hawkins testimony next week.

Next week's local second quarter CPI is again expected to show inflation well below that of the U.S. at an annual rate of just 0.6 percent, according to a recent Reuters survey, and if confirmed, yield differentials are expected to narrow sharply.

Australian/U.S. 10-year spread is closing in on last week's low of around 35 basis points, and the expected benign inflation report could see this tightening to major support at 25 b.p. New Zealand debt rebounded after Wednesday's weak performance and following a larger than expected fall in May retail sales.
